# `streaming_event_id_unique`

> Same event id with different content means a conflicting replay (exact replays are deduplicated).

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain | [streaming](README.md) |
| Layer | **silver** — evaluated by the `silver` gate |
| Model | `slv_streaming__playback_events` (`streaming_silver.slv_streaming__playback_events`) |
| Column | `event_id` |
| Check | `unique` |
| Severity | `error` — a violation **stops the pipeline** |
| Defined in | [dbt/models/streaming/silver/_silver.yml](../../../dbt/models/streaming/silver/_silver.yml) |

## What it checks

`event_id` is unique: no two rows share the same value.

## When it fails

The `silver` task of `medallion_streaming` fails, gold and `publish_gold` don't run, and the batch is never added to `streaming_gold`: consumers keep the batches published before. `quality_report` marks the run as blocked and sends the alert, if one is configured.

The rows that broke the rule in its latest evaluation are kept in `dq_audit.streaming_event_id_unique`.

## Tested by

Scenario **`duplicate_event_ids`**: same event_id delivered twice with different devices.

```bash
make generate DOMAIN=streaming SCENARIO=duplicate_event_ids BATCH=2026-10-20_duplicate_event_ids
make pipeline DOMAIN=streaming BATCH=2026-10-20_duplicate_event_ids
```

## Investigate

```sql
-- rows that broke the rule last time it ran
select * from dq_audit.streaming_event_id_unique;

-- history of the rule
select batch_id, status, failures, recorded_at
from dq_audit.rule_results
where rule = 'streaming_event_id_unique'
order by recorded_at desc;
```
